newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH SDP YOUTH GROUP WANTS MORE LEFTIST POLICY.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH SDP YOUTH GROUP WANTS MORE LEFTIST POLICY.

text.p: The Finnish Social Democratic Party's (SDP) youth organisation said in a statement on Tuesday that the SDP-led government's policies should be tuned more into line with the wishes of leftist voters.
It criticised the coalition's second biggest group, the moderate conservative party Kokoomus, saying it had attempted to steer government policy to match its own ideological goals.
"SDP is the biggest government party (and) must listen to its own parliamentary group," the youth organisation said.
"SDP must take a firmer grip of government policy," it said.

In a broad-based cabinet compromises were necessary, but not if the results went directly against opinions and values cherished by the party rank and file and members of the SDP parlimentary group, the youth organisation said.
It said it feared social democratic grassroots would not commit themselves to "all the right-wing decision that have now been made." It did not elaborate.
Looking ahead, it was high time for SDP to consider the terms for continued cooperation in government, the youths said.

"A socially fair policy requires a government with strong leftist representation. At the half-way point of the election period it is high time to repair government policy in such a way that decisions must not be forced down the throat of the own party," the SDP youth organisation said.
In a separate statement, the government said Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen will hold a news conference on January 30 at 1400/1200 GMT about the outlook for parliament's spring session.
The spring session is scheduled to start on February 3.
Lipponen's five-party left-right-green coaition took office in April 1995 and its term runs until 1999.
